source_text: Πρῶτον πάντων πίστευσον, ὅτι εἷς ἐστὶν ὁ θεός, ὁ τὰ πάντα κτίσας καὶ καταρτίσας καὶ ποιήσας ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ πάντα καὶ πάντα χωρῶν, μόνος δὲ ἀχώρητος ὤν. πίστευσον οὖν αὐτῷ καὶ φοβήθητι αὐτόν, φοβηθεὶς δὲ ἐγκράτευσαι. ταῦτα φύλασσε, καὶ ἀποβαλεῖς πᾶσαν πονηρίαν ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ καὶ ἐνδύσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν δικαιοσύνης καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ, ἐὰν φυλάξῃς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην.
pass_a_gloss: First of all believe that one is the God who created and arranged and made all things from not being into being and all things He contains but being alone uncontainable. Therefore believe in Him and fear Him and having feared exercise self-control. Keep these things and you will cast away all wickedness from yourself and you will put on all virtue of righteousness and you will live to God if you keep this command
pass_b_english: First of all, believe that there is one God. He created, arranged, and made all things out of nothing, and He contains all things while He alone is uncontainable. Therefore, believe in Him and fear Him; once you have feared Him, exercise self-control. Keep these things, and you will cast away all wickedness from yourself, put on every virtue of righteousness, and live for God — if you keep this command.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text of Mandate 1. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of the conditional clause and the participial phrase 'φοβηθεὶς δὲ ἐγκράτευσαι' (having feared/once you have feared) without altering the meaning or agency.
